The R1Pro of the official evaluation (``omnigibson/eval/r1pro.yaml``: controllers, base
mass, 30 Hz actions over 120 Hz physics) stands alone on a floor plane, watched by fixed
third-person cameras. Each run starts from the joint state the caller supplies, executes
native 23-D rows exactly as an episode would, and returns third-person frames and the
measured end state. There is no scene, object or task: nothing here reads a live episode.

symbols.name: look_at
symbols.doc: Quaternion (xyzw) of a USD camera (looks along -Z, +Y up) at ``eye`` facing ``target``.

symbols.name: robot_config
symbols.doc:
The evaluator's R1Pro config (``BatchedEvaluator._build_robot_config``), at the origin,
with only proprioception: the preview shows third-person views, not the robot cameras.

symbols.name: run
symbols.doc:
``measured``: the start state is the live episode's measured joints, not caller input,
so joint drift past a limit is clamped and reported like any measured hold.

summary:
Host-side owner of one BEHAVIOR-1K simulator subprocess (stdlib + msgpack + numpy only).

The subprocess runs ``python -m services.behavior.server`` in ``runtime/envs/behavior``;
this module never imports OmniGibson. Each process leases a private OmniGibson appdata
slot (kit caches, shader and texture caches, warp kernels): concurrent OmniGibson
processes must not share one, while sequential reuse keeps caches warm.

symbols.name: AppdataSlot
symbols.doc: Exclusive lease of one appdata directory, held by an open flock.

symbols.name: physical_gpu_index
symbols.doc: GPU ordinal or UUID -> nvidia-smi (PCI-ordered) index, which Kit's renderer uses.

symbols.name: simulator_environment
symbols.doc:
Environment for the simulator subprocess, mirroring scripts/behavior_env.sh.

CUDA sees only the simulator GPU (physics device 0), but Vulkan still enumerates every
GPU, so the renderer needs that GPU's physical index (ROBODOJO_RENDER_GPU).

symbols.name: BehaviorProcess
symbols.doc: One simulator process, its RPC client and its identity-checked requests.

summary:
Replay of a finished BEHAVIOR episode from its recorded actions, for its camera frames.

Runs only in ``runtime/envs/behavior``, like ``server.py``. It resets the episode's task
instance under the same evaluator configuration, steps every recorded
``<episode>/action_NNNNNN.json`` row in order, and saves the head and wrist RGB frames at the
requested steps and at the end. Physics need not repeat exactly, so every replayed base pose
is compared with the run's recorded one (``private_base_truth.jsonl``), and the replay's final
goal conditions with the run's goal report. ``replay.json`` records both comparisons and the
saved frames.

symbols.name: conditions
symbols.doc: Each goal option's final truth values, from a goal report.

summary:
Background reviews of finished BEHAVIOR exploration episodes (operator-side).

Reviews are part of closing an episode: the session's episode management (the supervisor
for single-environment episodes and rehearsals, the exploration pool for parallel ones)
reports each closed episode to the session's ``EpisodeReviews``, owned by its MCP service
(``services.controller.frontend``), so no dashboard is involved. While the operator has
reviews on, every closed exploration or rehearsal episode gets one review
(``services.behavior.analysis``):
- the operator record: ``<session>/operator-analysis/<episode_id>.json`` (0600), never
  readable by the agent;
- the agent's copy: ``review.md`` in that episode's own published run directory (the
  ``artifacts.directory`` its ``finish`` or ``rehearse`` reply named), which the agent reads
  read-only under ``runtime/autonomous_controller/runs/`` in its workspace. TASK.md says where.

Formal episodes are never reviewed. Gemini costs go to ``operator-analysis/usage.jsonl``
and never to the agent's own budget.

symbols.name: set_settings
symbols.doc:
Reviews on or off; detailed reviews also give the agent the partial score, the ground-truth
goal checklist and exact numbers.

symbols.name: _episode_artifacts
symbols.doc: Published trace and final images, and the exploration episode number, by episode ID.

symbols.name: _published
symbols.doc: A published file from its agent-visible logical path (``runtime/autonomous_controller/...``).

symbols.name: review_episode
symbols.doc: Review one finished episode row from ``review.episodes``; returns its operator record.

symbols.name: pending
symbols.doc: Finished, reviewable episode rows of a session that still need a review.

symbols.name: EpisodeReviews
symbols.doc:
Reviews each exploration or rehearsal episode of one session as it closes.

The session's episode management calls ``closed(episode_id)`` when an episode ends;
the review runs in the background (it takes about a minute) so closing never waits for
it. ``start`` catches up on episodes that closed while no MCP service ran.

symbols.name: closed
symbols.doc: An episode just closed: review it if reviews are on. Never raises into the caller.

symbols.name: _review
symbols.doc: Wait for the closed episode's simulator files, then review it (one retry on error).

summary:
R1Pro action/observation contract for the 2026 BEHAVIOR challenge (dependency-light).

Layouts mirror ``omnigibson/eval/utils/eval_utils.py`` (ACTION_QPOS_INDICES and
PROPRIOCEPTION_INDICES for R1Pro) and ``omnigibson/eval/r1pro.yaml``. Only challenge-track
inputs are exposed: RGB, depth and the 61-D proprioception, plus odometry integrated from
the proprioceptive base velocity. No world pose, object state or segmentation.

symbols.name: action_layout
symbols.doc: Agent-facing description of one 23-D action row.

symbols.name: joint_limit_violations
symbols.doc: Describe absolute joints outside the actual bounds; do not alter measurements.

symbols.name: validate_actions
symbols.doc:
Validate the entire batch before physics; clamp only epsilon-scale excursions.

``diagnostics`` receives a bounded correction report for the public reply.
The input is never modified, including when a later row is rejected.

symbols.name: decode_proprio
symbols.doc: Split the official 61-D proprioception into named fields.

symbols.name: hold_action
symbols.doc:
Action row that keeps the base still and holds the measured arm/trunk joints.

``grippers`` is the last commanded (left, right) gripper value: the measured finger
opening is not a command, so holding repeats the previous command.

symbols.name: bounded_hold_action
symbols.doc:
Clamp an internally generated measured hold, regardless of excursion size.

Measurements remain raw. Explicit agent targets use validate_actions instead.
Finiteness and normalized command checks still apply to these generated rows.

symbols.name: Odometry
symbols.doc:
Planar pose relative to the episode start, integrated from robot-frame base velocity.

Only the proprioceptive ``base_qvel`` ([vx, vy, wz] in the robot frame) is used, which
every challenge-track policy receives. Trapezoidal integration over one control period.

symbols.name: relative_goal
symbols.doc: Goal pose expressed in the odometry frame for a move relative to the current pose.

symbols.name: base_command
symbols.doc: Normalized base velocity toward ``goal`` (x, y, yaw) in the odometry frame.

summary:
BEHAVIOR-1K simulator process: one OmniGibson app, one task instance, one episode.

Runs only in ``runtime/envs/behavior``. The environment is constructed by the official
2026 ``BatchedEvaluator`` with the same configuration ``omnigibson.eval.eval`` builds
(partial scene load, human-demo-derived step limit, full-resolution RGB-D wrapper, fixed
evaluation seed), with a zero-action local policy because actions arrive over RPC.

symbols.name: preload_planner_libraries
symbols.doc:
Import the pinned warp and cuRobo before the Kit app starts: Isaac Sim bundles an older
omni.warp.core whose submodules would otherwise shadow warp-lang's and break cuRobo.

symbols.name: pin_render_gpu
symbols.doc:
Render on the simulator GPU. OmniGibson passes OMNIGIBSON_GPU_ID as both the CUDA
physics device and Kit's Vulkan renderer device; under CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES only the
former is remapped, so the renderer would land on physical GPU 0 and PhysX would find
no matching CUDA device. ROBODOJO_RENDER_GPU carries the physical index instead.

summary:
One BEHAVIOR-1K episode inside the OmniGibson process (runs in runtime/envs/behavior).

The official 2026 ``BatchedEvaluator`` (``num_envs=1``) owns environment creation, task
instance loading, settling, stepping and metrics, so this session reproduces the
organizers' evaluation exactly. The session adds the harness contract: identity-checked
RPC ops, challenge-track agent observations, start-relative odometry, and the trusted
operator files (``operator_state.json``, ``evaluation_outcome.json``, ``summary.json``,
``private_goal_report.json``)
that dashboards and formal scoring read. Nothing privileged is returned to the host
except inside those operator-only files.

symbols.name: _check_action_layout
symbols.doc: Fail fast if the robot's controller order differs from the published contract.

symbols.name: dof
symbols.doc: Robot joint indices driven by controller ``name`` (controllers are batched views).

symbols.name: _gripper_opening
symbols.doc:
Measured finger opening mapped onto [-1, 1] over the finger joint range, the
default output range of the smooth multi-finger gripper controller.

symbols.name: _execute
symbols.doc:
Run rows from an iterable (possibly closed-loop); keep every FRAME_STRIDE-th
frame plus the final one. Operator state is written once, at the end of the call,
or when the call fails after rows ran.

symbols.name: _record_after_failure
symbols.doc:
A call failed after rows ran: refresh the observation and the operator record, so
the next observe, the next hold action and the evaluation all start from this step.
The caller re-raises the original failure; a failure here is only logged.

symbols.name: base_move
symbols.doc:
Closed-loop planar move relative to the current odometry pose. Uses only the
integrated proprioceptive base velocity: no map, obstacles or world pose.

symbols.name: _object_orientations
symbols.doc: Task objects' orientations at reset, so the review can tell what tipped over.

symbols.name: _write_goal_report
symbols.doc:
Ground truth for the operator-side episode review: every grounded goal condition
with its initial and final truth, and the poses and extents of the objects involved.

summary:
TASK.md text for BEHAVIOR tasks: instruction, reviewed goal summary, BDDL goal and limits.

The challenge permits BDDL task definitions during evaluation, so the goal predicates are
given verbatim; ``task_rules/<task>.md`` holds the reviewed summary and the BDDL copied from
the pinned checkout. Partial-credit values stay in operator files; only detailed episode reviews report them.

symbols.name: task_context
symbols.doc: live_formal: for an agent formal copy. evaluation: False in live-copy mode.

symbols.name: review_level
symbols.doc: 'detailed', 'on' or None, from the operator's review setting for a session.

symbols.name: with_reviews
symbols.doc:
TASK.md text with its episode-reviews section replaced for ``level`` (None removes it).
rehearsals: False in live-copy mode, which has no bundle tools.

symbols.name: with_review_pointer
symbols.doc: AGENTS.md text with the review reminder before its Workflow section, only while reviews are on.

summary:
BEHAVIOR-1K 2026-challenge tasks (all 100; checked-in metadata; no dataset import).

``tasks.json`` is generated by ``scripts/generate_behavior_tasks.py`` from the pinned
2026 task-instance metadata and the upstream challenge gallery. Layout collections:
0 = train instances (exploration), 1 = public test instances 301-320 (held out).

symbols.name: instance_ids
symbols.doc: Instance IDs available in a layout collection, in canonical order.

symbols.name: layout_instance
symbols.doc:
Map a harness layout id to a BEHAVIOR instance id.

Exploration cycles through the train instances (layout ids wrap around); formal layout
ids index the 20 held-out public test instances and never wrap.

symbols.name: task_timeouts
symbols.doc: An episode ends at its native step limit: it has no wall-clock limit (episode_seconds None).

summary:
BEHAVIOR MCP tool schemas, host-side request validation and depth-pixel geometry.

Pure Python + numpy: safe to import in the host harness interpreter. Validation runs before
any RPC so a malformed request never touches the simulator.

symbols.name: validate_request
symbols.doc: Complete schema/shape validation before dispatch; raises RejectedBeforeAction.

symbols.name: pixel_to_base
symbols.doc:
Back-project one pixel of a linear-depth image into the robot base frame.

OmniGibson cameras follow the USD convention (looking down -Z, +Y up); pixel rays are
formed in the OpenCV convention and converted. ``depth_linear`` is distance along the
optical axis. Uses the median valid depth in a (2r+1)^2 window.

symbols.name: base_to_pixel
symbols.doc: Project a robot-base-frame point into a camera (inverse of pixel_to_base).

summary:
Simulator backends behind the shared harness: one registry entry per benchmark.

Pure configuration, like ``services.mcp_contract``: no simulator or heavy imports at module
load. Each benchmark is a peer: an entry here holds its data (robot tool names, robot facts,
setup defaults and fixed fields, capabilities), and its adapter module
(``services/<benchmark>/benchmark.py``) implements the hooks the shared harness calls. Shared
code dispatches through the entry and never compares benchmark names. The benchmark is fixed
at session creation; configurations saved before the field existed are RoboDojo (DEFAULT).

symbols.name: for_task
symbols.doc: The benchmark whose catalog has the task; task names are unique across benchmarks.

symbols.name: tool_benchmark
symbols.doc: The benchmark that owns a robot tool name, or None.

symbols.name: apply_fixed
symbols.doc: values with this benchmark's fixed setup fields.

summary: Token accounting from Claude Code's own transcripts, in the Codex usage shape.

symbols.name: UsageReader
symbols.doc:
Totals over the model responses in a Claude Code home, read incrementally (the dashboard
polls growing transcripts). Each response counts once: Claude Code writes one line per
content block, each with the response's usage so far, so its largest counts are kept.

symbols.name: home_usage
symbols.doc: Every conversation in a Claude Code home, subagents included.

symbols.name: compaction
symbols.doc:
A compaction's own model request, which the transcript records only as its boundary: it
reads the conversation (preTokens, from the prompt cache) and writes the summary
(postTokens). Measured against the relay's per-request log of the same session, these
match the requests the transcript lacks within 2%.

summary: Incremental, operator-only token accounting from Codex rollout JSONL.

symbols.name: home_usage
symbols.doc:
Every thread in a Codex home: summed session usage and the number of model responses
(one token_count event each).

summary:
Trusted, MCP-only execution backend for autonomous robot controllers.

Nothing in this package is exposed to the agent or its bundles; they reach it only
through MCP (auto_research_agent/api/runtime.py).
The existing interactive launchers are deliberately not changed by this backend.
Trusted adapter to existing MCP implementations, never exposed to the agent or its bundles.

symbols.name: make_backend
symbols.doc: The configured benchmark's trusted backend (RoboDojo when unspecified).

summary:
Operator-only post-hoc formal batch of an already rehearsed, frozen bundle.

Creates a new archive; never reopens or overwrites the source formal attempt.
No agent process, code edits, API credentials, or episode retries are involved.

symbols.name: exploration_layouts
symbols.doc:
Exploration layout seeds from `start` upward, wrapping to the collection's first
layout and cycling again when there are more episodes than layouts. Formal layouts
in the same collection are skipped, so they stay held out.

symbols.name: import_rehearsed_bundle
symbols.doc: Import evidence only after validating the source manifest and runtime.

summary: Host-only Gemini dollar accounting. Integer nanodollars avoid float drift.
Operator-owned configuration. No values are accepted from controller code.

symbols.name: retire_fields
symbols.doc: A saved configuration without the retired fields; a removed mode is a clear error.

summary: Host-side visual context for offline research workspaces, never simulator data.

symbols.name: provision_demonstration
symbols.doc:
record=False for an agent formal copy: the trial's descriptor belongs to its exploration.
demos_root (runtime/reference-demos) holds each benchmark's demonstration cache.

symbols.name: task_demonstration_context
symbols.doc:
live_formal: for an agent formal copy. bundles: code mode, whose rehearsals and formal
batch run the bundle without these images. Nothing when no demonstration is supplied.

summary: Complete public errors: the full message, with credentials, URLs and host directories removed.

symbols.name: redact
symbols.doc: Remove URLs, host directories and credentials; keep file names and the message.

symbols.name: describe
symbols.doc: One error as a line for a record: its type and its whole (redacted) message.

symbols.name: provider_body
symbols.doc: An HTTP error's response body, read once and kept on the exception.

symbols.name: public_failure
symbols.doc: The whole error the agent sees. Never replace it with a summary or a generic label.

symbols.name: provider_record
symbols.doc: Operator-only record of a failed provider call: the exception and the raw response body.

summary:
One formal episode of a parallel agent submission, in its own process.

The parent session supervisor keeps the Gemini key and the single session ledger;
this worker reaches both only through its inherited socket channel. It evaluates
exactly one held-out layout and is never restarted or retried by the parent.

symbols.name: Channel
symbols.doc: Worker side of the broker: one request/response at a time, never reused after failure.

symbols.name: WorkerSupervisor
symbols.doc: Charges the parent's session ledger instead of a private one.

symbols.name: serve_broker
symbols.doc: Parent side: expose only Gemini validation/execution and the shared ledger.

symbols.name: spawn
symbols.doc: Default worker factory: a detached process whose finally blocks own cleanup.

summary: Host-owned robot/API MCP for the native agent CLI (Codex or Claude Code) and its Python.

symbols.name: for_cli
symbols.doc: Tool definitions with image guidance for the agent CLI that reads them.

symbols.name: for_config
symbols.doc: Tool definitions adjusted to this session's agent CLI and mode.

symbols.name: load_configuration
symbols.doc:
The session's configuration with its task's current wall limits, as the launcher derives
them on every start: a session saved under an older limit (BEHAVIOR's, now none) runs and
resumes under the current one.

symbols.name: exploration_closed
symbols.doc: Budget spent with nothing running, or (code mode) the bundle already submitted.

symbols.name: closing_status
symbols.doc:
The carried folders (live-copy mode) and, once exploration is closed, the agent's
last steps before it is frozen.

symbols.name: carry_status
symbols.doc: Live-copy mode: what a later copy of the agent carries, and how full it is.

symbols.name: reply
symbols.doc: Small summary plus selected final frames.

symbols.name: serve_socket
symbols.doc:
Multiplex clients; execute every request on ONE main-thread dispatcher.

An idle Codex connection must not block a Python client. Evaluation calls
occupy this dispatcher, so development cannot act on their private episode.

symbols.name: Inventory
symbols.doc: Episode-independent tools: Gemini and pure pose math, no simulator.

summary: MCP-only capability gateway. A session is bound by its trusted transport.

symbols.name: episode_limits
symbols.doc: Public step budget from fields that sanitized() removes with the private layout data.

symbols.name: _handle
symbols.doc: Handle one actual MCP JSON-RPC message, with no client-selected identity.

summary: Credential-holding OpenRouter router, with no task/perception prompt logic.

symbols.name: validate_schema
symbols.doc: Bound schemas without resolving references or imposing a provider's dialect.

symbols.name: request_options
symbols.doc: OpenRouter inference fields only; function definitions are inert client data.

symbols.name: validate_image
symbols.doc: Validate supplied bytes without opening paths or fetching URLs.

symbols.name: image_token_bound
symbols.doc:
Prompt tokens reserved for one input image: an upper bound, not a tokenizer.

The provider bills about 1,100 tokens per image up to 1280 px (about 3,900 logged
single-image calls: median 980, largest 1,407 with the prompt text estimated); Gemini
models tile larger images at 258 tokens per 768 px tile. A reported cost above its
reservation closes the session's Gemini, so the bound keeps a wide margin over both.

symbols.name: load_key
symbols.doc:
Read an operator-selected private key file, or the supervisor environment.

Never discover credentials in agent bundles or persist them in trial state.

symbols.name: prepare
symbols.doc:
Validate inline images and preserve author prompts.

No external URLs, server tools, provider override, key or arbitrary HTTP fields
are accepted. The caller may supply any prompt and parse any response.

summary:
Operator-only parallel batch or migration; never retries a started layout.

Workers use the existing single-episode evaluator in independent processes. This
post-hoc evaluator has no API credentials; it is not the agent submission route.
Source results remain untouched. A durable, exclusive claim prevents re-migration.
Readable, offline progress views; JSON remains the evaluation source of truth.

Publish inspectable run files, not a new artifact API or manifest service.

Only this sanitized subtree is suitable for an agent's read-only file-view grant.
The private supervisor/native directories must never be exposed with it.

symbols.name: read_regular
symbols.doc: A regular file's bytes (never a link or device), refusing one over maximum bytes.

symbols.name: event
symbols.doc: Trace stays searchable; exact image-bearing responses get sidecars.

symbols.name: sequence
symbols.doc: Copy ONLY the existing safe frame sequence, never a simulator run dir.

symbols.name: finish_interactive
symbols.doc: Close a shared exploration trace; local source/logs stay in its workspace.

summary:
Runs a registered bundle in a bubblewrap sandbox: no network, no host sockets, credentials,
simulator or GPU; only the system, the agent's Python environment and the bundle's workspace.

symbols.name: ExecutionDeadline
symbols.doc: Cannot be swallowed by a tool's ordinary exception-to-MCP-error handler.

symbols.name: deadline
symbols.doc:
Bound even a blocked native MCP/provider call, not just the sandbox's CPU time. None sets no
limit of its own, but a timer set inside the block (a finalization limit) still raises.

symbols.name: wall_end
symbols.doc:
When a run must end: the tighter of its limit and the time left in its episode, as a
monotonic time; None when neither is set (the episode ends at its step limit).

symbols.name: finalize_within
symbols.doc: After the episode ends, give the run at most `seconds` more, within any limit left.

symbols.name: python_environment
symbols.doc: The agent's Python environment (the interpreter's prefix), by its real path.

symbols.name: output_bytes
symbols.doc: Bytes under `directory`, counting no further than just past `limit`.

symbols.name: frame_path
symbols.doc: Where a run's frames appear in its workspace (runtime/autonomous_controller/runs/<run>/frames).

symbols.name: command
symbols.doc:
The bundle's Python at the agent's own workspace path: a read-only scaffold with
the bundle at its project path, the runtime API, and a writable output directory.

symbols.name: limit
symbols.doc: preexec_fn: the sandbox's memory, file and core limits (inherited by everything in it).

summary: Private durable state and race-resistant, content-addressed bundles.

symbols.name: project_directory
symbols.doc:
A canonical project path in the agent's workspace (code/<name>...); never one that
shadows the runtime API or output.

symbols.name: directory_fd
symbols.doc: Pin every ancestor without following symlinks, including the root.

symbols.name: snapshot
symbols.doc:
Copy regular files only, then hash copied bytes, not mutable source paths.

Destination is supervisor-private and never mounted writable. No deserialization
or execution happens here. A failed partial snapshot is never registered.

summary: Durable trial/episode owner. Frontends must never instantiate a second owner.

symbols.name: qualifying_rehearsal
symbols.doc:
Shared evidence rule for admission and the operator's read-only display: the exact
bundle ran unattended to a clean, evaluated end. Task success is not required, since
formal scores give partial credit.

symbols.name: formal_outcome
symbols.doc: Task outcome from episode evidence, not a later infrastructure failure.

symbols.name: note_worker_exit
symbols.doc: Keep post-evaluation process health separate from the trusted task result.

symbols.name: left
symbols.doc: Seconds left of an episode's wall limit, or None when it has none.

symbols.name: stage_limit
symbols.doc:
The limit a timed-out episode is reported under: its wall limit, or without one, the
timed-out stage's own (environment startup, native evaluation).

symbols.name: _orphaned_worker
symbols.doc: Whether ``pid`` is a live formal worker of this session (a reused pid or a zombie is not).

symbols.name: _stop_orphaned_workers
symbols.doc:
Stop only live processes that are provably this session's formal workers, and wait until
they have exited: a worker saves its episode record while it stops, so its folder is final
only then, before recovery reads it or a resume moves it aside and plays its layout again.

symbols.name: _boundary
symbols.doc: Record a read-only boundary frame; never place its content in summary.

symbols.name: provider_log
symbols.doc:
Operator-only log of failed provider calls with their raw response bodies; never in a
run recording the agent can read.

symbols.name: start_interactive
symbols.doc: Start exploration shared by direct agent calls and development Python.

symbols.name: preflight
symbols.doc:
Every check run() makes before it consumes anything; no side effects.

Callers that must discard live exploration first run this, so a transient
failure (sandbox, bundle) leaves exploration open; they pass
live_episode_ok because they close the live episode right after.

symbols.name: submit
symbols.doc:
Close exploration on one bundle. Its formal batch runs later, isolated, after the
exploring agent has ended and been frozen (run_submission); the agent never sees it.

symbols.name: run_submission
symbols.doc: The submitted bundle's formal batch (bundle formal), run once after the freeze.

symbols.name: run_agent_formal
symbols.doc:
Play the formal schedule with live agent copies from a frozen checkpoint.

Runs after exploration closes, including after a bundle submission: both
drivers use the same held-out layouts, so their results pair episode by
episode. Every episode runs in its own worker process and child root.

symbols.name: resume_agent_formal
symbols.doc:
Finish an agent formal that was stopped before every layout had an outcome.

Episodes with an outcome stand. A stopped (interrupted) episode has none: its copy never
finished and it was never scored, so a fresh copy of the same frozen checkpoint plays that
layout from the start. The stopped attempt moves from the results to the batch's
interruptions record and its worker folder moves aside, so every reader of the results and
worker folders sees one episode per layout.

symbols.name: _formal_batch
symbols.doc: Run a formal batch; ``batch`` and ``done`` (1-based episodes with an outcome) resume one.

symbols.name: _record_formal
symbols.doc: Count one finished episode; an interrupted one is kept but never counted.

symbols.name: _worker_result
symbols.doc:
The worker's own episode record is authoritative.

A worker that started its episode but never finalized it counts as an error,
like a sequential timeout. One that never started an episode is a systemic
failure (spawn, preflight, bundle import), which interrupts the batch exactly
as it would in the sequential loop. A later nonzero worker exit is
recorded separately and cannot invalidate finalized task evidence.

symbols.name: _recover_parallel_formal
symbols.doc: After a supervisor crash: stop this session's workers and keep their evidence.

symbols.name: _run_parallel_formal
symbols.doc:
Run the reserved schedule on formal_workers concurrent episode processes.

Every layout is started at most once per run; a resumed agent formal skips the
episodes in ``done``, which already have an outcome. Gemini requests from all workers are
brokered here, so the session ledger and key stay in this process.
Episode numbers in batch state are 1-based, like formal_episode_index.

summary: Monotonic wall-time accounting; interrupted operations retain elapsed time.
Trusted, human-facing RoboDojo operator dashboard.
Read-only native camera snapshots shared by operator views; never robot RPC.

Read-only episode review: every simulator episode of a run and its trajectory video.

The native simulator records each episode's cameras as ``sim/sensors.mp4`` (25 fps,
cam_high | left wrist | right wrist side by side), so review streams those files
directly; nothing is re-encoded and nothing in the run is modified.

symbols.name: _results
symbols.doc: Controller records by native episode ID, from a session and its formal workers.

symbols.name: episodes

symbols.name: _rotation_to_quaternion
symbols.doc:
Decode one public rotation value to canonical unit ``wxyz``.

Euler input is fixed-axis/extrinsic XYZ in radians. Axis-angle input is a
rotation vector whose norm is the angle. Matrix input is flat row-major and
must be orthonormal with determinant +1. Non-zero quaternion input is
normalized; all output is sign-standardized to a non-negative scalar part.

symbols.name: _quaternion_to_rotation
symbols.doc: Encode canonical ``wxyz`` in one unambiguous public representation.

symbols.name: pose_math
symbols.doc:
Execute one validated, scene-independent high-level pose operation.

``compose_pose`` applies a local delta as ``T_base * T_delta``. An
environment delta adds translation directly in environment axes and
left-multiplies orientation as ``q_delta * q_base`` without rotating the
base position about the environment origin. ``relative_pose`` is the exact
inverse under the selected convention. ``format_target`` and
``extract_target`` translate between general poses and the named RoboDojo
EEF/cuRobo target fields without reading or advancing simulation.

summary:
Jinja rendering of trusted workspace sources.

Sources are markdown with Jinja statements on their own lines, e.g.

    {% if camera_geometry %}
    ...text for depth-capable profiles...
    {% else %}
    ...RGB-only text...
    {% endif %}

trim_blocks/lstrip_blocks drop the statement lines entirely, so rendered text keeps
the source's line layout. Unknown names fail the build (StrictUndefined).

Reusable passages are registered blocks (agent_blocks/blocks.toml) inserted with
{{ block("<id>") }} on a line of its own; the setup's facts, the recipe's `vocab`
and any keyword parameters are available inside a block. Every block a file uses
is recorded, so a build can report which blocks produced each file.
